== Fold and unfold Android devices during manual sessions

Manual sessions on supported foldable Android devices now include controls for folding and unfolding the device. Session Explorer also records these actions, making it easier to review how an app behaves across different screen configurations.

image::/foldable-icon.png[foldable icon in portal, 750]

=== Fold or unfold a device during a manual session

Use the *Fold device* or *Unfold device* control on the session toolbar to change the device's posture. The session stream and *Inspector* adjust to the active screen.

=== Review fold and unfold actions in Session Explorer

Session Explorer records each fold or unfold action as a timeline step, including a screenshot of the device in its corresponding posture.

Screenshots retain the screen dimensions of the active posture, and touch and swipe markers remain aligned with the captured screen.

This functionality supports book-style foldable devices, such as Galaxy Z Fold and Pixel Fold. Flip-style devices, such as Galaxy Z Flip, are not supported.

=== Considerations

* *Fold state:* The device retains its folded or unfolded state between sessions rather than resetting to a default state.
* *Automation:* Switching between folded and unfolded states is not currently supported during automated testing.

== Passcode entry support for iOS manual sessions

You can now enter device passcodes during iOS manual sessions, including passcode prompts for Apple Pay, Wallet, and the hidden apps folder.

=== Enter device passcodes during a manual session

When an iOS passcode screen appears, Kobiton Portal displays an interactive keypad overlay. Enter the passcode using the overlay or select *Auto-fill passcode* to use the device's configured passcode.

The *Passcode helper* menu on the session toolbar provides controls for showing or hiding the keypad and auto-filling the passcode.

=== Find devices that support passcode entry

The Devices page now includes a *Passcode* filter with *Supported* and *Not Supported* options.

Supported devices also display a passcode icon in card and list views, making them easier to identify before starting a session.

Passcode entry is supported when your organization has passcode (PIN) mode turned on and the device has a passcode configured.

For Apple Pay instructions, see xref:manual-testing:local-devices/use-apple-pay-in-manual-session.adoc[Use Apple Pay on iOS devices].

== Configure Appium AI settings across your organization

Users with the *ADMIN* role or the `org_setting.modify` permission can now configure Appium AI for the organization in Kobiton Portal, under *Settings* > *AI Settings*. New Appium sessions use the organization's LLM provider and locator settings without extra capabilities in test scripts.

With organization settings, you can:

* Turn Appium AI on or off for the organization.
* Set the API format, base URL, API key, model, locator strategy, and request timeout and retry interval.
* Override most organization settings for a single session with `kobiton:*` desired capabilities.

Changes apply to new sessions. Running sessions keep their existing settings. Organizations without saved settings continue to use the host defaults.

Appium AI is in Beta and is available on Private and Local devices only.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:appium-ai/configure-appium-ai-org-settings.adoc[Configure Appium AI settings for your organization].

// Source: KOB-54485 from PR #765

== Configure UiAutomator idle wait in Android automation sessions

Android Appium sessions now support the `waitForIdleTimeout` setting, which controls how long UiAutomator waits for an app to become idle before searching for elements.

Set `appium:waitForIdleTimeout` when starting a session, or change the setting during a session using the Appium Settings API.

Setting the timeout to `0` skips the idle wait, helping prevent element searches from failing in apps that continuously update their interface.

The default remains 10 seconds when no value is specified.

For details, see xref:automation-testing:capabilities/available-capabilities.adoc#_waitForIdleTimeout[waitForIdleTimeout].

== Improved results and session visibility in the Kobiton MCP server

The Kobiton MCP server now provides more information about validation progress and search results, along with improvements to interactive automation.

* *Validation progress:* AI assistants can distinguish between scans that are still processing and completed results, including accessibility, crash, response time, and network payload validations.
* *Search results:* Device searches now report the total number of matching devices. Pagination limits also help manage results for test cases, test suites, test runs, and user input events.
* *UI inspection:* The `automate` plugin 1.15.0 now uses a compact UI tree by default during interactive automation, with full page source available on request.

For details, see xref:ai:mcp/ai-plugin-mcp-ref.adoc[Kobiton AI plugin and tools reference].

// Source: KOB-55322 from PR #726

== Reset stuck device states with the Kobiton API

Organization administrators can now use the `POST /v2/execute-admin-tasks` API to reset devices that remain in an incorrect state, such as a device that appears in use after its session has ended.

The new `RESET_DEVICE_STATE` task resets the recorded state of one or more devices and returns the result for each device.

The reset does not end active sessions or cancel reservations. Devices become available for new sessions when their host machine next reports their state.

// Source: KOB-55366 from PR #710

== List installed apps on devices with the Kobiton API

The new `GET /v2/devices/{deviceId}/installed-apps` and `GET /v2/devices/udid/{udid}/installed-apps` APIs return applications installed on a private device, including apps installed manually or through mobile device management (MDM).

Results include each application's bundle ID, name, version, and build version. An optional parameter also returns the Kobiton app repository version ID when a matching version exists.

== Improved element inspection and interaction in Appium sessions

Several fixes improve how Appium sessions identify and interact with elements:

* *iOS 26 location permissions:* Automation scripts can now locate and interact with buttons on location permission alerts, including *Allow Once*, *Allow While Using App*, and *Don't Allow*.
* *iPad web sessions:* Appium Inspector now displays the correct XML hierarchy for each step of an iPad automation session started without an app, such as a Safari session.
* *Android web views:* Fixed an issue on Android 13 and later where screens containing web views did not display their complete XML hierarchy, preventing element searches and interactions.
* *Element attributes:* The WebDriver Get Element Attribute command now returns `null` when an element does not have the requested attribute, instead of returning an error.
* *Set element text:* Appium automation sessions now support the `mobile: setText` command on Android and iOS. Previously, using this command returned a "not implemented" error.

== Improved reliability for iOS and iPadOS devices

Several fixes improve device connections, cleanup, and health checks on iOS and iPadOS devices.

* *Device connections:* Fixed intermittent Developer Disk Image (DDI) mounting failures on newer iOS devices, including iPhone 18 models running iOS 26.4 and later. This also resolves failures when a DDI is already mounted.

* *Device cleanup:* Device cleanup now correctly resets settings such as time zone, language, and HTTP proxy on devices with newer iOS and iPadOS Settings layouts.

* *Device health checks:* When an XCTest runner fails to start, the device health check now reports the underlying runner error instead of an unrelated passcode error. The device also retains its passcode when the failure is unrelated to passcode configuration.

// Source: KOB-55400 from PR #724

== Restored crash reporting in Session Explorer

Session Explorer now displays app crashes and their crash logs for sessions on Android and iOS devices, including manual, Appium, and API sessions. Previously, crashes that occurred during these sessions were not captured, leaving no crash logs available for review.

// Source: KOB-55471 from PR #737 (sessions with no recorded steps)
// Source: KOB-55496 from PR #744 (XCUITest null-labeled steps)

== Session Explorer: Improved handling of sessions without recorded steps

Sessions without recorded steps now open on Session Overview instead of an empty Session Explorer. The *Explorer* tab displays "Explorer is not available for this session."

This also fixes an issue where XCUITest sessions displayed steps labeled `null` with no screenshots.

// Source: KOB-55419 from PR #753

== Improved app installation error messages in manual sessions

When an app installation fails during a manual session, Kobiton Portal now displays the error reported by the device instead of replacing it with a potentially misleading explanation.

For example, iOS signature verification failures now display `ApplicationVerificationFailed` instead of an AS-500 error about Kobiton certificate signing. Installation errors that include a Kobiton error code continue to display that code.

// Source: KOB-55472 from PR #739

== Improved access to running XCUITest session details

The `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` and `GET /v2/sessions/{id}` APIs now return session details while XCUITest native framework sessions are running. Previously, these requests returned an HTTP 500 error before the session's test report and video became available.
